bullets.title: NVDA: Raymond James raises PT to $352; Groq ramps; OpenAI Jalapeno chip threat; credit risk flagged
bullets.body: Raymond James raised NVDA to $352 from $330 (Strong Buy), citing CPU acceleration to potentially 5% of revenue by 2028. NVIDIA's Groq 3 (acquired $20B Dec-2025) is in full production with Samsung Foundry ramping ~10k wafers/month. MS TMT raises concern on ~$200B all-in credit exposure by CY28 via lease backstops and revenue-sharing models, rating NVDA credit Neutral. Separately, SemiAnalysis reports OpenAI's Jalapeno inference chip outperforms NVDA on top open-source models, pressuring the stock off highs. Hedgeye notes NVDA broke Trade level at $218/Trend at $208 with risk range $192-$230 and takes no position ahead of earnings.

bullets.title: AMD: Raymond James upgrades to Strong Buy, raises PT to $641 on server CPU growth
bullets.body: Raymond James upgraded AMD from Outperform to Strong Buy and raised its price target to $641 from $565. The firm expects the server CPU market to reach $201B by 2030 at a 44% five-year CAGR. Morgan Stanley separately notes AMD's agentic AI CPU ramp in 2027 will foreshadow NVIDIA's CoWoS packaging demand surge.

bullets.title: MRVL: Street expects Q2 beat; consensus $2.72B rev, $0.93 EPS; DC growth FY forecast raised to 50%
bullets.body: Marvell reports F2Q27 on 8/27; consensus expects $2.72B revenue, 58.8% gross margin, and $0.93 EPS, all in-line with guidance. The Google partnership is viewed as positive but raises concentration questions; DC growth FY forecast was raised to 50% with interconnect accelerating 70%+ Y/Y on 800G/1.6T products. Options imply ~10.5% move. Rosenblatt upgraded MRVL to Buy in pre-market.

bullets.title: META: Hatch AI agent platform launching imminently at up to $199.99/month; Watermelon model in October
bullets.body: META is rolling out 'Hatch,' an agentic AI platform, in late August/early September at up to $199.99/month with higher usage limits and task automation. A 'Watermelon' model is targeted for October. Citi and Morgan Stanley both flag this as a meaningful monetization catalyst; WhatsApp AI-agent platform also in development.

bullets.title: GOOGL: MS raises TPU pricing to ~$27B/GW, targets $84B/$108B cloud revenue in 2027/2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised GOOGL TPU 1P sale estimates to ~$27B per GW (from $20B) at 30% gross margin (from 20%), modeling $84B and $108B in TPU-related Cloud revenue for 2027 and 2028, up ~35% vs prior. Cloud is expected to reach ~50% of total EBIT by 2028, with Brian Nowak targeting $18-$20 EPS in 2028. GOOGL is currently trading at 17x 2026 EPS, valuations down 36% vs TTM average.

bullets.title: AVGO: Bearish trend flagged; one of 3 stocks driving 25% of SPY's recent down day
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough notes AVGO is showing bearish Trade/Trend signals and was one of only three stocks accounting for 25% of yesterday's SPY decline alongside NVDA and MU. JPM's Harlan Sur maintains AVGO as a top pick on custom ASIC momentum but flags elevated credit risk from mega AI debt financing backstops (5-year CDS up 28bps).

bullets.title: SNOW: Citi raises PT to $395 from $320 on strong partner checks and AI Build momentum
bullets.body: Citi raised Snowflake's PT to $395 from $320, expecting a Q2 revenue beat of 4%+ with a 2-3pt FY27 raise and acceleration to high-30%s guidance by Q3. CoCo momentum and the AI Build model are cited as ~7pts of FY27 growth contribution.

bullets.title: CIEN: MS FQ3 preview — backlog reaccelerating >$600M; NVDA fiber build an incremental driver
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains CIEN Equal-Weight at $490 PT. FQ3 backlog is expected to reaccelerate above $600M driven by multi-year AI optical cycle demand; LITE pump-laser shipments up >80% Y/Y support durable demand. NVIDIA's 8,000+ mile long-haul fiber build is a real incremental opportunity but sized at potentially <$1B total contribution. Supply constraints remain the near-term governor.

bullets.title: AAPL: Tim Cook exits as CEO within one week; M6 (2nm) and M5 Ultra chips launched
bullets.body: Apple has launched the M6, its first 2-nanometer chip with 12-core CPU/GPU and up to 170GB/s unified memory bandwidth, and the M5 Ultra with a quad-die UltraFusion architecture offering up to 80-core GPU and 1.2TB/s bandwidth (50% more than M3 Ultra). Separately, Tim Cook has less than one week remaining as CEO.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybertruck prices hiked $5K amid demand concerns
bullets.body: Tesla raised U.S. Cybertruck prices by $5,000, with the dual-motor AWD model moving to $74,990 and the full AWD to $84,990. The price increase coincides with ongoing demand concerns and recent recalls.

bullets.title: CRWD: DA Davidson bullish ahead of Fal.Con; trades at 79x FCF vs 39x for growth peers
bullets.body: DA Davidson reports strong channel checks showing CRWD continuing to dominate alongside PANW as platform consolidation remains intact. Shares have outperformed IGV by 76% and CIBR by 41% YTD. However, valuation at ~79x FCF vs 20-30%+ growth peers at ~39x creates a challenging near-term setup. Analyst attending Fal.Con user event 9/1-9/2 and expects more typical ARR upside in Q2.

bullets.title: MRVL, NVDA, AVGO, MU: WFE forecasts raised to $223B in 2027, $254B in 2028 by MS
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) forecasts to $223B for 2027 (+37% YoY) and $254B for 2028 (+14%), driven by DRAM bit supply growth of 38% in 2027 vs 24% in 2025 and HBM capacity expansion. This is a positive read-through for semiconductor capital equipment and memory players.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS maintains Buy; McCoy acquisition expands Edge into midmarket SAP; 2027 M&A upside
bullets.body: Accenture is acquiring McCoy, a Dutch SAP consultancy with ~380 professionals, as its 9th Q4 2026 deal (33 YTD vs 13 in Q4 2025). UBS notes Accenture raised FY26 M&A spending to ~$9B from an initial $3B guide, with 150bps inorganic revenue contribution held flat—implying 2027 upside. UBS maintains Buy with $275 PT.

bullets.title: AMZN: $530M Project Tetromino spend on AI warehouse automation targeting 2.5x efficiency
bullets.body: Amazon plans to spend $530M through 2029 on Project Tetromino, deploying AI-driven warehouse automation expected to deliver 2.5x efficiency gains. JPM flags AWS remains compute-constrained through 2026 despite a $220B capex budget, with contracted backlog at $496B on 5-year terms.

bullets.title: WMT: Hedgeye shifts to Short after 20%+ stock decline since May peak despite Q2 upside
bullets.body: Hedgeye, which had WMT as a Best Idea Long entering 2026, shifted to Short a quarter ago. Despite Q2 upside and raised guidance on sales/EBIT/EPS, shares fell the most in 4+ years and are now down 20%+ from the May peak. Concerns center on whether AI investment delays promised margin gains, tariff rebate impacts on 2026-2027 projections, and valuation vs. the Supercenter rollout era.

bullets.title: NFLX: Ad exec Jon Whitticom departing; ad-supported tier still >60% of new subscribers
bullets.body: Citi flags Netflix advertising executive Jon Whitticom is departing. Despite the leadership change, advertising remains a high-margin incremental revenue stream, contributing more than 60% of new subscribers in ad-supported markets.

bullets.title: RH: Web traffic decelerates sharply to +low-20s in August MTD from +low-40s in July
bullets.body: Citi's retail web traffic tracker shows RH decelerating materially to the low-20% range in August MTD from the low-40% range in July, the most notable deceleration in the tracked cohort. Overall US retail web traffic averaged +26.6% in August Week 3, slightly below Week 2's +29.8%.

bullets.title: INTU: Citi cautions F4Q expectations look elevated; investor poll at 10.9% FY27 growth
bullets.body: Citi warns that Intuit's FY27 revenue growth expectations—at 10.9% y/y per investor poll, in-line with consensus—may still be elevated heading into the print. The analyst is cautious that guidance could reset lower.

bullets.title: DKNG: JPM organizing G2E investor meetings Sept 28-29 with CFO Alan Ellingson presenting
bullets.body: JPMorgan is hosting management meetings at the G2E Las Vegas conference on September 28-29, with DraftKings CFO Alan Ellingson and finance team presenting on September 29 at 2:00 PM PT. DraftKings has a market cap of $13.3B.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex exceeds cash flow; $1.2T expected in 2027 vs ~$1T operating cash flow
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and JPM both flag that hyperscaler AI capex is projected to exceed $1.2T in 2027 vs approximately $1T in operating cash flow, with >$3.1T in disclosed off-balance-sheet commitments across hyperscalers, NVDA, and AVGO enabling third-party AI infrastructure financing. CSPs (AWS, GCP, MSFT) are described as compute-constrained through 2026 despite record capex budgets.
